result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is the better answer. It lays out the journey as a persona grid with rows for what the member does, asks, feels and where they touch the studio, so staff can see what Kiln & Co. owns at each stage (website times page, plan page, follow-up email, front desk, shelf system, firing). It also says openly which parts are guesses or interpretation. A is clean, faithful to the six conversations and easy to read, but it is mostly a list of findings without much feeling or studio ownership. One weakness in B: only two moments get the orange highlight, so the out-of-date times, feeling in the regulars' way and month-three doubt appear only in the 'what goes wrong' row. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is a proper journey map built around a single new member. It has rows for what they do, ask, feel and where they touch the studio, so staff can see what the studio owns at each step: the website times page, the follow-up email, the kiln, the shelf system and the front desk. It also flags its own guesses honestly. B's cards are clean and highlight every pain point more evenly, but they are mostly a regrouped list of the findings, with little of the member's thinking or feeling and fewer studio touchpoints. A's denser grid also uses orange for only two moments, so some bad moments are marked less strongly.
